description: A sine LFO with a wavefolder on it: the folder shapes an external signal, or the built-in sine when nothing is patched in

params.text: Sets the rate of the built-in sine, 0.01Hz to 5Hz, and becomes a multiplier of the rate measured at SYNC while a cable is patched there
Multiplies the signal before folding, 1 to 10, so it crosses more fold points the further clockwise it goes
Shifts the signal before folding, -2.5 to 2.5, moving it across the fold points
Chooses the fold: triangular reflects the signal back each time it passes a fold point, sinusoidal passes it through a sine function
Sets the range read at the input jack: unipolar subtracts 5V first, treating 0-10V as centred on 5V, bipolar takes -5V to 5V unchanged
Sets the range of both outputs: unipolar gives 0-10V, bipolar gives -5V to 5V

inputs.text: The signal to be folded; with nothing patched here the fold is skipped and OUT carries the built-in sine unchanged, despite the tooltip calling this jack normalled to the LFO
A rising edge above 2V restarts the built-in sine and sets its rate from the time between edges, which LFO Freq then multiplies

outputs.text: The built-in sine after folding, folded whatever is patched to the input jack
The folded input signal, or the built-in sine with no folding applied when nothing is patched to the input jack
